newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FRENCH TITLE SHOWDOWN NEITHER SIDE DARE LOSE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FRENCH TITLE SHOWDOWN NEITHER SIDE DARE LOSE.

text.p: Failure is something both sides are refusing to contemplate with so much at stake when Monaco and Paris Saint-Germain clash in the key match of the French league championship on Sunday.
Neither coach is prepared to announce his line-up until the last minute for fear of his opposite number taking the slightest advantage.
Confidence has been the word on the lips and in the minds of players determined that this season they will make up for the failures of the previous seasons in their bid for the first division title.
"We're going to play to win... In our heads we have remained positive. Let's think of victory, the title. A team like Paris can only have that in their heads," said PSG's Brazilian Rai.
After a string of poor results, will heads roll if PSG lose and fall a massive seven points behind leaders Monaco?
A poker-faced manager Ricardo, who had his resignation turned down by PSG after last week's 6-1 humiliation by Juventus in the European Super Cup, is not giving his feelings away.
But PSG chief executive Michel Denisot said: "I don't think there'll be a resignation, I don't want to believe that."

Monaco's Brazilian Anderson, lifting a silence he imposed on himself earlier in the week, said he would not be affected by the PSG syndrome that spoilt his game when the two sides met in Paris and drew 0-0 in September.
Linked with PSG since the off-season, Anderson complained of the pressure in the build-up to the Parc des Princes match badly affecting his concentration.
Now more settled in Monaco and saying he will stay if they win the title, Anderson fears PSG's ability to react positively to their adverse situation.
"They're a big club and we know that in this kind of match a big club can find its identity again," Anderson said.

With his compatriots in the PSG side including his idol Rai in mind, Anderson added: "They have the players with the mentality to surpass themselves ... and allow PSG to rediscover their earlier confidence and we must beware of that."
Anderson said the match would be decided in midfield where both sides have gifted technical players.
Monaco welcome back Belgian Enzo Scifo from injury with a new attitude to contribute to Monaco's bid for a first league title since 1988.

"I'm back to my best, I no longer have any apprehension. If I had any worries due above all to the difficulty of finding my rhythm... the intense preparation for this re-start (after the winter recess) has borne its fruits," Scifo said.
Normally accustomed to the leading role in the side, Scifo said the team has been playing very well in his absence and he is "keen to behave like a worker."
"There are players capable of taking the creative role, Ali Benarbia does so marvellously and I like playing beside him as long as I can contribute in another role.
"I have the feeling today of being in a great club, there is everything to achieve... everyone is concentrated, we are conscious of our strength " he said.
Defender Emmanuel Petit, also back from injury, compared the current Monaco side with that which last won the title under Arsene Wenger in 1988.
"We have become aware as a team that we can and must win something this year and we know today we're better than the team of the last few years," he said.

"Only the side in which I made my debut with (Glenn) Hoddle and (Dominique) Battiston can compare in terms of the new spirit," added Petit, who said he has been linked with Tottenham Hotspur in the past and would like to play in England.

"The match will be hot, that's for sure. I just hope that what's at stake won't predominate over a good game as is too often the case in this kind of match," said Petit, who is expected to play in a four-man defence.
Meanwhile, PSG's other Brazilian Leonardo is fighting to get fit for the match after a bad bout of flu.
Probable teams:
Monaco - 1-Fabien Barthez; 2-Patrick Blondeau, 5-Franck Dumas, 4-Martin Djetou, 6-Emmanuel Petit; 15-Sylvain Legwinski, 7-John Collins, 8-Ali Benarbia, 10-Enzo Scifo; 9-Anderson, 12-Thierry Henry.
Paris St Germain - 1-Bernard Lama; 17-Jimmy Algerino, 6-Paul Le Guen, 4-Bruno N'Gotty, 22-Didier Domi; 8-Vincent Guerin, 19-Jerome Leroy, 15-Benoit Cauet, 10-Rai; 7-Leonardo, 21-Cyrille Pouget.
